To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) We propose an adaptive similarity-based learning framework that is applicable across domains.

(i) a data driven framework can be used to learn similarity functions that generalize better than existing similarity functions and (ii) a diversity based heuristic can be used to select landmark points for similarity based learning.

(i) we propose a novel framework for similarity-based learning, (ii) we show that this framework unifies and improves existing approaches, (iii) we propose an algorithm for learning a goodness function for similarity-based learning from data, and (iv) we show that our approach consistently outperforms state-of-the-art approaches on similarity-based learning as well as benchmark classification tasks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: How to define the goodness of a similarity function with respect to learning?
learning similarity-based classifiers.
the following questions: (i) Can the goodness of a similarity/distance function be defined in terms of the learning task at hand?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our framework is the first to propose an adaptive similarity-based learning approach that can be used in a variety of domains.
our method is a general and flexible approach to similarity-based learning that can be applied in many domains and problems.
our approach outperforms all the existing methods on a wide range of problems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a general and flexible framework that is capable of learning similarity functions for a variety of problems and tasks.
we propose a framework that learns the best possible goodness criterion for a similarity function and then learns a classifier from it.
our framework allows us to learn the best similarity function for a given problem, learn a good classifier using that similarity and learn a good subset of landmarks for our classifier.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of similarity functions can have a profound effect on the performance of similarity based classification algorithms.
the choice of a similarity function is a crucial aspect of learning and that it should be learned from the data.
the choice of a (dis)-similarity function can be learned from data and this can be exploited for effective learning.
